arxiv-2103-01132.title: General Bayesian L 2 L^{2} calibration of mathematical models
arxiv-2103-01132.creator: Antony M. Overstall
arxiv-2103-01132.description: Abstract A mathematical model is a representation of a physical system depending on unknown parameters. Calibration refers to attributing values to these parameters, using observations of the physical system, acknowledging that the mathematical model is an inexact representation of the physical system.

arxiv-2209-10603.title: Charge Symmetry Breaking Effects on Neutron Beta Decay in Non-Relativistic Quark Models
arxiv-2209-10603.creator: Jacob W. Crawford and Gerald A. Miller
arxiv-2209-10603.description: Abstract A formalism for the study of charge symmetry breaking (CSB) effects is discussed and used to analyze the effects of charge symmetry breaking on neutron beta decay. The effect of including CSB reduces the beta decay matrix element by an amount on the order of 10 − 4 10^{-4} , a value much larger than the previous estimate.

arxiv-2407-00251.title: Leveraging Fixed-Parameter Tractability for Robot Inspection Planning
arxiv-2407-00251.creator: Yosuke Mizutani, Daniel Coimbra Salomao, Alex Crane, Matthias Bentert, Pål Grønås Drange, Felix Reidl, Alan Kuntz, Blair D. Sullivan
arxiv-2407-00251.description: Abstract Autonomous robotic inspection, where a robot moves through its environment and inspects points of interest, has applications in industrial settings, structural health monitoring, and medicine. Planning the paths for a robot to safely and efficiently perform such an inspection is an extremely difficult algorithmic challenge.

arxiv-2501-03334.title: FEL Gain Enhancement in an Optical Klystron Journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods A
arxiv-2501-03334.creator: Anahit H. Shamamian, Hayk L. Gevorgyan, Lekdar A. Gevorgian
arxiv-2501-03334.description: Abstract A formula for the spectral distribution of intensity of radiation from a system of gap-separated undulators is derived. Due to the constructive addition of radiation fields formed in undulators, the line shape of the spontaneous radiation at zero angle is narrowed.

arxiv-2509-12732.title: A Novel Recurrent Neural Network Framework for Prediction and Treatment of Oncogenic Mutation Progression
arxiv-2509-12732.creator: Rishab Parthasarathy \ORCID 0000-0002-8982-9469, Achintya Bhowmik
arxiv-2509-12732.description: Abstract Despite significant medical advancements, cancer remains the second leading cause of death, with over 600,000 deaths per year in the US. One emerging field, pathway analysis, is promising but still relies on manually derived wet lab data, which is time-consuming to acquire.

arxiv-2601-05032.creator: Steven Rivetti, Gabor Fodor
arxiv-2601-05032.description: Abstract The temporal evolution of the propagation environment plays a central role in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. A slow-time evolution manifests as channel aging in communication links, while a fast-time one is associated with structured clutter with non-zero Doppler. Nevertheless, the joint impact of these two phenomena on ISAC performance has been largely overlooked.

pmc-10671108.title: Oxidative Stress and Antioxidant Defense in the Heart, Liver, and Kidney of Bat Species with Different Feeding Habits
pmc-10671108.creator: Francielly Dias Pereira, Diego Antonio Mena Canata, Tiago Boeira Salomon, Fernanda Schäfer Hackenhaar, María João Ramos Pereira, Mara Silveira Benfato, Pabulo Henrique Rampelotto, David Della-Morte
pmc-10671108.description: The aim of this study was to compare the oxidative metabolism of four neotropical bat species with different feeding habits and investigate the relationship between their feeding habits and oxidative status. In terms of oxidative damage, our findings revealed major differences among the four bat species.

pmc-11321752.title: Incorporating Patient Values in Large Language Model Recommendations for Surrogate and Proxy Decisions
pmc-11321752.creator: Victoria J. Nolan, Jeremy A. Balch, Naveen P. Baskaran, Benjamin Shickel, Philip A. Efron, Gilbert R. Upchurch, Azra Bihorac, Christopher J. Tignanelli, Ray E. Moseley, Tyler J. Loftus
pmc-11321752.description: Background:Surrogates, proxies, and clinicians making shared treatment decisions for patients who have lost decision-making capacity often fail to honor patients’ wishes, due to stress, time pressures, misunderstanding patient values, and projecting personal biases. Advance directives intend to align care with patient values but are limited by low completion rates and application to only a subset of medical decisions.

pmc-11445922.title: Complete mitochondrial genome and phylogenetic analysis of Chloris chloris (Passeriformes: Fringillidae)
pmc-11445922.creator: Xiaodong Gao, Jincheng Liu, Xinyue Zhang, Tong Zhao
pmc-11445922.description: In this study, we employed high-throughput metagenomic data to assemble the mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) of the European greenfinch (Chloris chloris; Linnaeus 1758). The circular mitogenome was 16,813 base pairs (bp) in length, containing 13 protein-coding genes (PCGs), 22 tRNA genes, 2 rRNA genes, and 1 control region. The base composition of the mitogenome is 30.6% A, 30.7% C, 14.

pmc-11479055.title: Integrative Modeling and Experimental Insights into 3D and 4D Printing Technologies
pmc-11479055.creator: Angel Cabrera Pereira, Vasudev Vivekanand Nayak, Paulo G Coelho, Lukasz Witek, Babak Eslami, Kamran Fouladi, Michèle Kanhonou, Hamid Reza Vanaei
pmc-11479055.description: This review focuses on advancements in polymer science as it relates to three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) printing technologies, with a specific emphasis on applications in the biomedical field. While acknowledging the breadth of 3D and 4D printing applications, this paper concentrates on the use of polymers in creating biomedical devices and the challenges associated with their implementation.

pmc-11493239.title: Trends in NHANES Biomonitored Exposures in California and the United States following Enactment of California’s Proposition 65
pmc-11493239.creator: Kristin E Knox, Megan R Schwarzman, Ruthann A Rudel, Claudia Polsky, Robin E Dodson
pmc-11493239.description: Background:The prevalence of toxic chemicals in US commerce has prompted some states to adopt laws to reduce exposure. One with broad reach is California’s Proposition 65 (Prop 65), which established a list of chemicals that cause cancer, developmental harm, or reproductive toxicity. The law is intended to discourage businesses from using these chemicals and to minimize consumer exposure.

pmc-11504250.title: Potential Ecological Distribution of the Beetle Agrilus mali Matsumura (Coleoptera: Buprestidae) in China under Three Climate Change Scenarios, with Consequences for Commercial and Wild Apple Forests
pmc-11504250.creator: Yanlong Zhang, Hua Yang, Aerguli Jiamahate, Honglan Yang, Liangming Cao, Yingqiao Dang, Zhaozhi Lu, Zhongqi Yang, Tohir A Bozorov, Xiaoyi Wang, Leon G Higley
pmc-11504250.description: Simple SummaryThe apple buprestid beetle Agrilus mali is a pest that can cause serious harm to various domestic apples and many species of Malus. Currently, it is distributed in 17 provinces of China. After spreading from Shandong province to Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, it has caused great damage to the local wild apple resources.

pmc-11515726.title: Close relationships with caregivers as protective factor for the mental health and functioning of war-affected Congolese youth
pmc-11515726.creator: Florian Scharpf, Roos Haer, Tobias Hecker
pmc-11515726.description: BackgroundSupportive social connections are a crucial determinant of the mental health and adjustment of youth in conflict-torn regions. Conflict-affected youth face particular risks to their well-being due to high levels of trauma exposure and perpetration of violent acts as members of armed groups and post-conflict discrimination.

pmc-12398939.title: Age-driven changes in the layer hen reproductive microbiome are associated with lay performance
pmc-12398939.creator: Kathryn M Ellwood, Ashley E Kramer, Aditya Dutta
pmc-12398939.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Eggs are a globally important food source and integral to optimal poultry production. Understanding the microbial ecology of the hen reproductive tract is essential for improving both food safety and reproductive efficiency. While the oviduct has been shown to harbor a continuous microbial community, this study is the first to demonstrate the presence of microbiota on the hen ovary surface, suggesting that the ovary is an extension of the oviductal microbial continuum.

pmc-12930214.title: Comparative Efficacy of Silver Diamine Fluoride and Sodium Fluoride in Managing Early Childhood Caries: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-12930214.creator: Atiyeh Farahi, Nazieh Abdollah Kookhi, Benika Abbasi, Morteza Sharifi, Majedeh Nami, Yousef Moradi
pmc-12930214.description: BackgroundEarly childhood caries (ECC) is a prevalent condition in preschool children that can impair nutrition and development. Comparative evidence on silver diamine fluoride (SDF) versus sodium fluoride (NaF) for arresting ECC remains limited.ObjectivesTo compare the efficacy of topical SDF and NaF in arresting ECC lesions and to evaluate effects on decayed, missing, and filled surfaces (DMFS).

pmc-12990058.title: Home-Based Immersive Virtual Reality to Improve Motor Performance in Children and Adolescents With Developmental Coordination Disorder: Crossover Study
pmc-12990058.creator: Mohammed Alharbi, David Harris, Helen Dodd, Greg Wood, Gavin Buckingham
pmc-12990058.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChildren with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) experience motor difficulties that limit daily activities and reduce physical activity enjoyment. pmc-13497264.title: Alignment-free prediction of cross-reactivity in influenza A (H3N2) anticipates antigenic drift
pmc-13497264.creator: Alpha Forna, Lambodhar Damodaran, Christian E Gunning, Parnian Rahimi, Aarya Venkat, Natarajan Kannan, Rebecca Kondor, Justin Bahl, Pejman Rohani, John M Drake, Tommy Tsan-Yuk Lam
pmc-13497264.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Since its introduction in 1968, Influenza A (H3N2) has undergone continuous antigenic evolution, necessitating frequent vaccine updates. To predict antigenicity and characterize antigenic drift without multiple sequence alignments, we present FluEmbed, a computational framework that leverages protein language models. FluEmbed accurately quantified the antigenic impact of viral evolution from RNA sequences, achieving strong predictive performance against hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay titers (Spearman correlation: ρ = 0.67–0.80).
